paragraphs: O-CITY is an automated fare collection platform for public transport operators and municipalities, and the payment technology behind it comes from BPC. The platform digitalises the payment process end-to-end, and travellers use a mobile or a payment card rather than paper tickets. Citizens and tourists can pay with smart cards, contactless Visa, MasterCard or UnionPay, mobile wallets, and QR codes.

These pages say the platform is sold to transport agencies, governments and merchants for self-service digital ticketing across their cities. For operators, account-based ticketing is described as reduced costs, improved efficiency and easier fare management. Fares can be based on route, type of transport or service, or traveller status such as student or senior.

Deployment options include on-premise, PaaS, SaaS or fully managed operations, on existing transport or merchant terminals. A case study on the platform page describes Bishkek moving away from the use of cash. Another case study describes a Ministry of Transport automating public transport fare collection.

quote.text: To empower transport operators and governments to provide an easy, secure and transparent city payment experience.
